attribution.note: Marcus's own updated assessment ('Two years later...') in his own post. It is not a quotation of someone else.

semantics.note: A present-tense observation. The 'perhaps' only hedges the Meta exclusion, not the main claim that open models are a few months behind.

contract.note: Reading open source as open-weight and 'a few months' as 2 to 6 months is an ordinary plain reading. The Jan–Jun 2026 window is a reasonable choice for 'now'.

evidence.note: Epoch's independent ECI analysis, published May 29, 2026 (before the post), finds a 4-month average lag over Jan–May 2026.
Same analysis: under the stricter test the lag is 6 months, still within 'a few months'. Epoch notes the true gap may be understated.

reviews.rationale: Epoch's independent measurement puts the open-weight lag at 4 months on average (6 months under a stricter test) for Jan–May 2026. That fits 'only a few months behind'. Epoch's caveat that the gap may be understated does not push it toward a year or more.

attribution.note: Marcus's own assertion in Part II of his post.

semantics.note: A two-part present-tense observation about providers and customers. The normalisation keeps both parts and adds nothing.

contract.note: The contract judges intent from actions and spending, which is a defensible ordinary reading. The customer half depends on using aggregate revenue at the leading provider as the measure of willingness to pay per token.

evidence.note: Anthropic ended flat-rate subscription use for third-party agents in April 2026.
GitHub's own changelog shows all Copilot plans moved to usage-based billing on June 1, 2026. This is a disclosure of its own pricing action.
Anthropic paused its June 15 billing change, so agent use stayed on subscriptions. This partly cuts against the provider half. The same report says enterprises are cutting spend.
S-1 reporting: $16.3B revenue in H1 2026 against $4.6B in all of 2025. That points to sharply rising spending, though it is H1 rather than Q2 alone and is not split by billing type.
Most lab revenue is per-token enterprise spending. Some firms (Meta, Uber, Walmart) capped use, which is partial support for customer reluctance.

reviews.rationale: Provider half holds: Anthropic (April) and GitHub (June) moved away from flat-rate access for heavy use, though Anthropic paused a further change. Customer half fails under the contract: spending at the leading usage-based provider rose sharply in H1 2026, even though some firms capped spend.

attribution.note: Marcus speaking in an interview transcript that he published in his own post.

semantics.note: 'I think' qualifies 'has a problem'. 'Burning money the fastest' is stated flatly, and 'right now' makes it a present observation.

contract.note: Reading 'fastest' as the largest absolute net cash burn is an ordinary reading. The quarter, perimeter and accounting basis are evaluator choices, which the contract flags.

evidence.note: OpenAI's 2025 cash burn ($8B, reported from private sources). Wrong period and no comparison with rivals.
Anthropic's S-1 cash flows cover H1 2026, not Q1, and do not give a comparable burn figure.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no comparable Q1 2026 cash-burn figures for OpenAI and each named rival. OpenAI's quarterly report could not be read, and the Anthropic and 2025 OpenAI figures are for different periods. The ranking cannot be settled.

attribution.note: Marcus speaking in an interview transcript that he published in his own post.

semantics.note: Two linked observations: providers run at a loss, and agent use deepens the loss. The normalisation is faithful.

contract.note: In context (the buffet metaphor), reading 'bigger loss' as agents costing more to serve than flat prices recover is fair. The result still depends on that per-usage reading rather than a company-wide margin.

evidence.note: OpenAI's Q1 2026 operating loss was $9.3B (reported from shareholder documents, unaudited).
GitHub's stated reason for the change: multi-hour agent sessions cost far more to serve than chat at the same price.
In 2025 Anthropic limited 24/7 Claude Code use because it was financially costly.
OpenAI's company-wide gross margin rose from 33% to 39%. It does not isolate agent economics.

reviews.rationale: OpenAI ran a large operating loss in Q1 2026. GitHub and Anthropic both said or acted on agent use costing much more than flat prices recover. OpenAI's improved gross margin is company-wide and does not show agent use was profitable, so it is context, not contradiction.
